### Candidate 1: Feminist Structure Signal

* **Title**: MoMA 举办《Taking Back Our Space》特展：将 1970 年代女性主义身体摄影档案与当代跨媒介实践并置 / MoMA Presents 'Taking Back Our Space: Photographic Perspectives'
* **Source URL**: `https://www.moma.org/calendar/exhibitions/5707`
* **Publication Date**: September 20, 2026 (Exhibition runs through May 2, 2027; featured in current October 2026 programming)
* **Proposed Section**: Feminist Structure Signal
* **Verified Facts**:
  * Organised by Roxana Marcoci (The David Dechman Senior Curator) and Caitlin Ryan (Assistant Curator) at MoMA's Paul J. Sachs Galleries.
  * Centers on German artist Marianne Wex's 1977 photographic study *Let's Take Back Our Space: 'Female' and 'Male' Body Language as a Result of Patriarchal Structures*, which MoMA acquired in its entirety in 2018.
  * Pairs Wex's historic archive with contemporary works by seven artists shown at MoMA for the first time: Nona Faustine, Martine Gutierrez, K8 Hardy, Yuki Kihara, Joiri Minaya, Paulina Olowska, and Wendy Red Star.
  * Accompanied by a 176-page paperback exhibition catalogue published by MoMA.
* **Relevance to Muki**: Directly links 1970s feminist visual sociology, body posture archives, and spatial politics to contemporary intersectional, queer, and Indigenous self-representation strategies.
* **Duplication Assessment**: New. Not included in recent issues.

### Candidate 2: Visual Culture Signal

* **Title**: 伦敦摄影师画廊开幕 Sanlé Sory 彩色摄影回顾展：首次公开 1980–90 年代布基纳法索日常与音乐文化档案 / The Photographers' Gallery Presents 'Sanlé Sory: Colour Years'
* **Source URL**: `https://thephotographersgallery.org.uk/whats-on/sanle-sory-colour-years`
* **Publication Date**: October 14, 2026 (Exhibition runs through February 21, 2027)
* **Proposed Section**: Visual Culture Signal
* **Verified Facts**:
  * Curated by Taous Dahmani at The Photographers' Gallery in London, in collaboration with the Sanlé Sory Archive and Florent Mazzoleni.
  * Features Sory's rarely seen color photography, restored directly from original box negatives stored for decades in Bobo-Dioulasso, Burkina Faso.
  * Documents studio portraiture, youth fashion, and local music culture (including original Volta Jazz record sleeves) from the mid-1980s through the 1990s following post-independence political shifts.
  * Accompanied by the photobook *Volta Colour*, published by GOST Books in October 2026 (£45).
* **Relevance to Muki**: Provides a crucial primary photographic source on West Asian/African vernacular image history, photobook publishing, and studio archive restoration outside Western-centric histories.
* **Duplication Assessment**: New. Not included in recent issues.

### Candidate 3: China / East Asia Signal

* **Title**: 2026 集美·阿尔勒公布重磅单元方案：具本昌策展韩国当代静物摄影，重新审视 AI 时代的图像真实性 / 2026 Jimei × Arles Announces Special Focus on Korean Contemporary Photography and Curatorial Engine
* **Source URL**: `https://www.threeshadows.net/news/`
* **Publication Date**: October 15, 2026
* **Proposed Section**: China / East Asia Signal
* **Verified Facts**:
  * Three Shadows Photography Art Centre and Jimei × Arles announced details for the 2026 edition (opening November 20, 2026 in Xiamen).
  * The "Asian Film/Photo Focus" (亚洲影汇) section is curated by South Korean photographer Koo Bohnchang (具本昌) under the title *Objects in Oscillation* (振荡中的物件).
  * Features eight South Korean photographers (including Chung Heeseung, Jo Seongyeon, Kim Kyoungtae, and Zo Sunhi) examining objecthood, materiality, and image authenticity amidst AI technologies.
  * Unveiled the winning exhibition project *Embers* (余火) by curator Wang Liquan (王立秋) under the Chanel-supported Curatorial Project.
* **Relevance to Muki**: Bridges East Asian contemporary photographic research, material image politics in the age of generative AI, and emerging Chinese/Korean curatorial frameworks.
* **Duplication Assessment**: New. (While SIPF was featured on Oct 19, this announcement specifically highlights Jimei x Arles' 2026 curatorial program and Koo Bohnchang's exhibition focus).

### Candidate 4: AI Research / Creative Tech Signal

* **Title**: Reflection AI 开源 501B 参数 Beam 模型：首个专为 Agent 与长文本推理设计的开源混合专家模型 / Reflection AI Releases Open-Weight 501B Beam Model for Agentic Reasoning
* **Source URL**: `https://huggingface.co/blog/reflection-beam`
* **Publication Date**: October 16, 2026
* **Proposed Section**: AI Research / Creative Tech Signal
* **Verified Facts**:
  * US lab Reflection AI released the weights for `Beam` on Hugging Face under the Apache 2.0 license.
  * Architecture uses a sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) design with 501 billion total parameters and 23 billion active parameters per token, featuring a 1-million-token context window.
  * Specifically engineered for complex coding, structured tool calling, multi-agent orchestration, and long-horizon reasoning tasks.
  * Released with day-0 integration across Hugging Face Transformers v5.20.1, vLLM, SGLang, and an open-source command-line coding harness (`Mirror CLI`).
* **Relevance to Muki**: Marks a structural shift in open AI infrastructure, giving creative technologists and researchers access to local, high-parameter agentic reasoning models without proprietary API gatekeeping.
* **Duplication Assessment**: New. (Differentiates from recent ComfyUI workflow updates by focusing on open-weights agent infrastructure).

### Candidate 5: Archive / Long Read / Opportunity

* **Title**: 德国威斯巴登艺术协会启动 2026/27“Follow Fluxus”奖学金招募：提供 1 万欧元资助、三月驻留与个展支持 / Nassauischer Kunstverein Wiesbaden Opens Call for Follow Fluxus Scholarship 2026/27
* **Source URL**: `https://www.kunstverein-wiesbaden.de/en/follow-fluxus/the-scholarship/call-for-application-follow-fluxus-scholarship-202627.html`
* **Publication Date**: October 2026 (Application deadline: November 1, 2026, 23:59 CET)
* **Proposed Section**: Archive / Long Read / Opportunity
* **Verified Facts**:
  * Awarded annually since 2008 by Nassauischer Kunstverein Wiesbaden and the Hessian state capital Wiesbaden.
  * Offers an international artist a €10,000 grant, a 3-month rent-free residency (June 1 – August 31, 2027) in the Kunsthaus Wiesbaden studio house (70.88 m² space), and a solo exhibition at the Kunstverein.
  * Open to national and international visual and performing artists with a completed art degree or documented self-taught artistic achievements.
  * Requires project proposals that engage with the ideas/practices of the Fluxus movement and transform them for contemporary 21st-century practice.
* **Relevance to Muki**: Directly supports Muki's research into performance archives, media archaeology, interdisciplinary experimental art, and institutional grant opportunities.
* **Duplication Assessment**: New. Not included in recent issues.
